Thanks for the suggestions. I have reviewed the pinned documentation (#4997) and the mentioned issues, but my problem appears to be distinct:

- **Regarding #32483 (System shortcut conflicts):** 
`ctrl+p` is neither a Windows system-level shortcut, nor is it a default shortcut for Windows Terminal, PowerShell (pwsh), CMD, or Git Bash that would cause an OS-level interception. 

- **Regarding #37151 (Custom hotkey overridden):** 
Issue #37151 seems to refer to custom keybinds not working. In my case, `ctrl+p` is the **default** keybind for `command_list` out of the box. I am not trying to set a custom shortcut; rather, the default one has completely stopped responding. Furthermore, reassigning `ctrl+p` to any other action also fails.

To summarize, this doesn't seem to be an OS shortcut conflict or a custom config issue, but rather a specific regression in how v1.18.2 captures the `ctrl+p` key combination on Windows (as it worked perfectly in v1.17.20).

Confirming this is still present in **v1.18.2** (tag `v1.18.2`, commit `70b56a0a9`), and adding a source-level root cause + fix direction. This is the same underlying behavior as the auto-closed #25811 (global, not project-scoped) and #19536 / #19436 (multi-instance clobbering) — none of which were fixed before the inactivity bot closed them.

## Root cause

The TUI prompt-recall history is persisted to a **single global file with no project/session/directory key and no locking**:

```
$XDG_STATE_HOME/opencode/prompt-history.jsonl
```

Every concurrent `opencode` TUI process reads from and writes to this same file regardless of project/dir/session.

- Path is keyed only by the global state dir + a constant filename — `packages/tui/src/prompt/history.tsx:52-53`:
  ```ts
  const paths = useTuiPaths()
  const historyPath = path.join(paths.state, "prompt-history.jsonl")
  ```
  `paths.state` = `global.state` = `$XDG_STATE_HOME/opencode` (`packages/tui/src/app.tsx:260`, `packages/core/src/global.ts`), identical for every invocation.
- The persisted record `PromptInfo` (`history.tsx:9-25`) stores only `input`/`mode`/`parts` — **no project or session id**, so it can't be filtered even in principle.
- Read path loads the whole file unfiltered on mount (`history.tsx:54-61`); write path appends on every submit (`history.tsx:85-108`, called from `packages/tui/src/component/prompt/index.tsx:1121,1273`); recall bindings are Up/Down → `history.move()` (`config/keybind.ts:199-200,402-403`; `component/prompt/index.tsx:879,915`).

That fully explains the arrow-up recall showing another session's prompts.

## Secondary defect (the "#19536" clobbering)

The over-cap branch rewrites the whole file from the process's **stale in-memory** snapshot (`history.tsx:103-104`), overwriting entries other instances appended since this process last read — a lost-update race. No lock / atomic write on this path (`packages/tui/src/util/persistence.ts:12-20`), even though the repo already has `Flock` (`packages/core/src/global.ts`, `Flock.setGlobal({ state })`) and `writeJsonAtomic` (`persistence.ts:22-33`, unused here).

## Scope / not-scope

- Session **transcripts are not affected** — DB rows are correctly isolated by `project_id`/`directory`. I verified two concurrent sessions in different projects: distinct `project_id`, distinct `directory`, distinct message counts. Only the prompt-recall file leaks.
- Same global-file design affects siblings under `paths.state` and may show the same bleed: `prompt-stash.jsonl` (`prompt/stash.tsx:36`), `frecency.jsonl` (`prompt/frecency.tsx:42`), `model.json`/`session.json` (`context/local.tsx:164,420`), `kv.json` (`context/kv.tsx:15`) — i.e. the umbrella #19436.

## Suggested fix direction

1. **Scope per project.** Key the filename by `project.id` (already available via `useProject()`, `packages/tui/src/context/project.tsx:49-50,78-80`), falling back to a hash of worktree/cwd for unsynced/non-git dirs; e.g. `paths.state/prompt-history/<key>.jsonl`. Resolve reactively — `project.id` is briefly `undefined` before the first `sync()` (`project.tsx:38-53`), so don't capture a single `const` at init.
2. **Fix the race.** Prefer append-only on the hot path + enforce the 50-entry cap lazily on read (the mount-time self-heal at `history.tsx:58-60` already trims). If a rewrite is kept, guard with `Flock` and/or a JSONL-preserving atomic write.

Tests worth adding: two-projects-concurrent (leak), same-project interleaved over the 50-entry cap (race), non-git dir and `cd`-within-repo (isolation vs continuity).

## Workaround for affected users

Give each instance its own state dir:
```bash
export XDG_STATE_HOME="$HOME/.local/state/oc-$(basename "$PWD")"
```

> * [[Bug] Keyboard shortcuts don't work when Chinese IME is active #24192](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/24192): [Bug] Keyboard shortcuts don't work when Chinese IME is active — same symptom reported as a bug with technical analysis of the root cause

Thanks for the suggestions. I am aware that #16252 and #24192 were successfully resolved in PR #22041. That PR did a great job fixing the recognition of modifier key combinations (like `ctrl+x`) while a non-English IME is active.

However, my feature request addresses a different scenario: the **sequential workflow AFTER the `leader` key is successfully triggered**.

While PR #22041 fixed the initial `leader` keystroke (`ctrl+x`), the subsequent key in a leader sequence is usually a single, bare letter (e.g., just pressing `a` or `c`). Because it is a bare letter without modifiers, the OS IME naturally intercepts it and opens the candidate window.

This request is specifically asking for a feature to temporarily bypass the IME (or auto-switch to English) **only while OpenCode is in the "waiting for leader key sequence" state**. This would prevent users from having to press `Enter` to pass the raw letter through the IME just to complete a shortcut.

To summarize, this is a workflow enhancement for sequential keybinds (chords), not a duplicate of the modifier key bug fixed in PR #22041.
